Create a hexbin plot.

Source: R/hexbin_plot.R
hexbin_plot.Rd

A hexbin plot is a two-dimensional histogram: the x/y plane is tiled with a grid of regular hexagons, every observation is assigned to the hexagon it falls into, and each hexagon is colored by the number of observations it contains. It is a readable alternative to a scatter plot when there are too many points to see individually (overplotting), because dense regions remain distinguishable instead of turning into a solid blob.

The look is inspired by the hexbin transform of the Observable Plot library: light gridlines, a sequential color scale with a continuous legend, and an optional mode where the hexagon size (area) also encodes the count. Binning is done in pixel space, so the hexagons are always regular regardless of the units of x and y.

The plot is interactive: hovering a hexagon outlines it, marks its count on the color legend and (when tooltip = TRUE) shows a tooltip with the bin count, its share of all observations, and the x/y range covered by the hexagon.

Usage

hexbin_plot(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  binWidth = 12,
  sizeByCount = FALSE,
  colorPalette = "YlGnBu",
  reverseColors = FALSE,
  colorScale = c("linear", "sqrt", "log"),
  legend = TRUE,
  legendTitle = "Count",
  tooltip = TRUE,
  hover = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  opacity = 1,
  stroke = "white",
  strokeWidth = 0.5,
  grid = TRUE,
  gridCol = "#e5e5e5",
  xtitle = NULL,
  ytitle = NULL,
  xtitleFontSize = 13,
  ytitleFontSize = 13,
  title = NULL,
  titleFontSize = 16,
  xFontSize = 11,
  yFontSize = 11,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bgcol = "white",
  axisCol = "black",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The data frame containing the variables to consider.

x

The name of the numeric column mapped to the horizontal axis.

y

The name of the numeric column mapped to the vertical axis.

binWidth

The radius of each hexagon in pixels (distance from its center to a corner). Larger values give fewer, coarser bins. Defaults to 12.

sizeByCount

Logical. When TRUE, the area of each hexagon is also proportional to its count (the largest bin fills its cell), in addition to the fill color. Defaults to FALSE.

colorPalette

The name of a D3 sequential color interpolator, without the "interpolate" prefix (e.g. "Viridis", "Blues", "YlGnBu", "Magma", "Turbo"). Defaults to "YlGnBu".

reverseColors

Logical. Whether to reverse the direction of the color palette. Defaults to FALSE.

colorScale

How counts are mapped to colors: "linear" (default), "sqrt" or "log". Use "sqrt" or "log" when a few very dense bins wash out the rest.

legend

Logical. Whether to draw the continuous color legend. Defaults to TRUE.

legendTitle

Title of the color legend. Defaults to "Count".

tooltip

Logical. Whether to show a tooltip when a hexagon is hovered. Defaults to TRUE.

hover

Logical. When TRUE (default), hovering a hexagon outlines it and marks its count on the legend.

animate

Logical. When TRUE (default), hexagons grow into place with a short staggered entry animation on first render.

opacity

Fill opacity of the hexagons (0 to 1). Defaults to 1.

stroke

Stroke color of the hexagons. Defaults to "white".

strokeWidth

Stroke width of the hexagons in pixels. Defaults to 0.5.

grid

Logical. Whether to draw light gridlines behind the hexagons. Defaults to TRUE.

gridCol

Color of the gridlines. Defaults to "#e5e5e5".

xtitle

Optional. Title of the x-axis. Defaults to the value of x.

ytitle

Optional. Title of the y-axis. Defaults to the value of y.

xtitleFontSize

Font size of the x-axis title. Defaults to 13.

ytitleFontSize

Font size of the y-axis title. Defaults to 13.

title

Optional. Title of the chart.

titleFontSize

Font size of the chart title. Defaults to 16.

xFontSize

Font size of the x-axis tick labels. Defaults to 11.

yFontSize

Font size of the y-axis tick labels. Defaults to 11.

font

The font family used for all text. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bgcol

Background color of the SVG. Defaults to "white".

axisCol

Color of axis lines, ticks, labels and titles. Defaults to "black".

width

Optional. The width of the SVG output.

height

Optional. The height of the SVG output.

Value

An SVG hexbin plot.

Examples

# Old Faithful geyser: eruption duration vs waiting time
hexbin_plot(
  data     = faithful,
  x        = "waiting",
  y        = "eruptions",
  binWidth = 14,
  xtitle   = "Waiting time to next eruption (min)",
  ytitle   = "Eruption duration (min)",
  title    = "Old Faithful eruptions"
)



# 10,000 diamonds: carat vs price, with a log color scale
library(ggplot2) # for the diamonds dataset
set.seed(1)
dsample <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 10000), ]

hexbin_plot(
  data         = dsample,
  x            = "carat",
  y            = "price",
  binWidth     = 8,
  colorPalette = "Viridis",
  colorScale   = "log",
  xtitle       = "Carat",
  ytitle       = "Price (USD)",
  title        = "Diamond price by carat"
)



# Hexagon size encodes the count as well as the color
set.seed(42)
pts <- data.frame(
  a = c(rnorm(1500, 0, 1), rnorm(800, 3, 0.6)),
  b = c(rnorm(1500, 0, 1), rnorm(800, 2, 0.6))
)

hexbin_plot(
  data         = pts,
  x            = "a",
  y            = "b",
  binWidth     = 13,
  sizeByCount  = TRUE,
  colorPalette = "Magma",
  reverseColors = TRUE,
  title        = "Two bivariate normal clusters"
)
